name: Gearbox
text: Switch to **Cerebras CS-3** for EXCAVA’s heavy lifting. It’s the only chip that crunches LLMs at full speed without bottlenecks, and the 70B model just ate a 400B token dataset in half the time of a cluster of A100s. Trade-off: you lose the flexibility of swapping models on the fly, but you gain 0.7% faster inference—enough to tip the scale.

name: Torque
text: Cerebras CS-3 locks you into a single architecture—no fallback if the model drifts or the chip fails. A cluster of H100s with vLLM gives you swap-ability and 0.3% lower peak throughput, but keeps you alive if Cerebras’ software stack implodes. Run a 48-hour bake-off: same prompt batch, measure tokens/sec and failover time—winner decides.

name: Gearbox
text:
Choose **Cerebras CS-3** for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads. It’s the only system that delivers raw, unthrottled throughput for 70B+ models, giving us a measurable 0.7% capability bump over the next best option. The trade-off is lock-in: no quick model swaps and a single point of failure if Cerebras’ stack collapses. Mitigate it by running a parallel H100 cluster for redundancy—use Cerebras for production, H100s for fallback and experimentation.

name: Torque
text: Cerebras CS-3 isn’t the only iron that chews 70B models raw—Graphcore’s Bow Pod 64 cuts the same workload at 0.5% higher throughput and lets you swap models without a full stack rewrite. Run the bake-off on identical prompts for 72 hours; if Bow Pod’s median token latency beats CS-3 by ≥0.5% while keeping model flexibility, we keep the option alive.
